title: Find things fast
summary: Quick Open, searching, and the command palette.

steps.title: Quick Open
steps.say: Big projects have lots of files. To jump to one, press **Ctrl+P**. A little box opens at the top. Click somewhere in the editor first, so it hears your keys.

steps.title: Type part of a name
steps.say: Type `about` (the start of a file's name) and press **Enter** to open it. You don't have to remember where it lives.

steps.title: Search everything
steps.say: Press **Ctrl+Shift+F** (hold Ctrl and Shift, tap F). The left panel turns into **Search**: it looks for words inside **all** your files.

steps.title: Search for a word
steps.say: Type a word from your about.txt in the search box. Matches appear below, grouped by file. Click one to jump straight to it.

waitFor.hint: search for a word you wrote.

steps.title: Back to your files
steps.say: Press **Ctrl+Shift+E** to get back to the Explorer.

steps.title: The command palette
steps.say: Can't find a button? Press **Ctrl+Shift+P**. This is the **command palette**: type what you want to do (try `save`) and it lists the matching commands. Press **Esc** to close it.

steps.title: Your shortcuts
steps.say: Ctrl+P finds a file by name. Ctrl+Shift+F finds words everywhere. Ctrl+F finds words in the file you're in. Ctrl+Shift+P finds any command. Together they save you a lot of clicking.
